question.problem: A sample ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ of $n$ shirts is drawn from a population. The population has shirts of two different sizes, $8$ and $10,$ distributed in the ratio $1:3.$ Determine the smallest sample size required so that the standard error of the mean is less than $0.5.$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population variance ${\sigma }^{2},$ then

$$
\text{E}[\overset{―}{X}]=\mu ,\,\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]=\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n},
$$

and the standard error is given by

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[\overset{―}{X}]}=\frac{\sigma }{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

We're told that the shirts in the population have sizes $8$ and $10,$ and these are distributed in the ratio $1:3.$ Therefore, to compute the population's mean and variance, we can consider a population consisting of $1+3=4$ shirts only with the following sizes:

$$
8,\,10,\,10,\,10.
$$

Therefore, the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\frac{1}{4}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(8+3\cdot 10) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(8+30) \\  & =\frac{38}{4} \\  & =9.5,\end{aligned}
$$

and the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\frac{1}{4}{\sum }_{i}{x}_{i}^{2}-{\mu }^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}({8}^{2}+3\cdot {10}^{2})-{9.5}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(364)-90.25 \\  & =91-90.25 \\  & =0.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the population standard deviation is $\sigma =\sqrt{0.75},$ and we have that 

$$
\text{SE}[\overset{―}{X}]=\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{n}}.
$$

We require that the standard error is less than $0.5.$ Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{n}} & <0.5 \\ \sqrt{n} & >\frac{\sqrt{0.75}}{0.5} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{{0.5}^{2}}} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{0.25}} \\ \sqrt{n} & >\sqrt{3} \\ n & >3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest sample size is $n=4.$
